correctness.rationale: The initial pairwise vertex-normal inequalities are equivalent to 2n adjacent inequalities because the corresponding directed edge arguments advance through a single turn; a scalar supporting projection has a single valley and returns to its starting maximum. Invertible adjacent tangent coordinates identify the translation quotient with the nonnegative kernel of a rank-two closure matrix whose n tangents each occur twice. Each coordinate hyperplane is a facet via transfer of a positive coefficient between duplicated columns. Extreme rays are exactly the support-minimal positive dependencies of that matrix: antipodal pairs and three-direction circuits positively enclosing the origin. The cyclic-gap count yields the stated parity formulas. The packaged checker independently tests closure, every original inequality, facet witnesses and active ranks for n=3..12 (1480 enumerated rays), without substituting finite tests for the general proof.

The two constructions have distinct ambient dimensions and face counts; stronger deformation-cone theorems do not imply this new object-specific classification.

originality.rationale: The August 2026 primary source introduces the same cone and discusses individual redundancies, but the inspected relevant full-text portions did not include an exhaustive planar facet and ray classification or regular-grid formula. The closest deformation-cone literature concerns a distinct fan-preserving Minkowski-summand parameter space; a dimension/facet/ray comparison rules out treating it as equivalent. Multiple actual semantic searches under vertex-normal, polygon-chain, positive-circuit and deformation-cone aliases yielded no exact matching statement. Standard positive-circuit theory and any inherited local redundancy are explicitly acknowledged. Residual older-literature risk persists; the literature search is not a uniqueness certificate.
residual_risks: Similar cyclic cone classifications may exist in older mechanical self-stress, allowable-sequence, normal-fan, or oriented-matroid terminology.
The completely classical positive-circuit characterization, considered in isolation, is not new; the new contribution is the application and exhaustive exact spectrum.
The related graphical zonotope article was compared at statement/abstract level, not exhaustively line-by-line.

value.rationale: The cone is intrinsic to a new finite-dimensional convex-body approximation scheme. Replacing n(n-1) comparisons by a provably minimal 2n facet system has a direct computational meaning; moreover the complete generator classification and nonmonotone cubic parity law describe the previously unspecified extremal geometry for an entire natural family, not an arbitrary small numerical slice. No downstream result is conjecturally asserted as proved.
